card.name: Partway through long medical terms
card.fires_on: Mid-word pieces of long clinical terms such as hepat(ocellular), anaphyl(actoid), palp(able) and pap(ules). It also fires on a comma or bracket right after an abbreviation expansion.

modes.label: Split medical words
modes.description: The first pieces of a long medical word that is still unfinished, such as hepat, palp, pap or act in anaphylactoid.
modes.example: clinically manifests as<< pap>>ules, plaques, or nodules

modes.label: Abbreviation lists
modes.description: A comma or opening bracket just after a spelled-out term and before its abbreviation or next entry.
modes.example: Drug Reaction with Eosinophilia and Systemic Symptoms<< (>>DRESS) Drug Reaction with Eos

card.writes: It promotes odd word-start pieces and suppresses 'involve' words, so it does not clearly add anything meaningful.
card.plain: It lights up in the middle of a long medical word that has not finished yet, like anaphylactoid or papules.
